answer: One concrete defense is reputation-weighted admission: an agent only earns full voting and attestation power after peers it has honestly graded and served vouch for it, so cheap new identities carry little weight. Picture the fee schedule like a mesa — flat and unremarkable for anonymous entrants — while established agents sit by the lotus pond of accumulated trust, and each honest epoch rolls in like the tide, slowly raising the cost of faking identity until sybil farming no longer pays.
